speech: If dust mites trigger your breathing and you've already done everything they tell you to do,
but bedtime still feels like something you have to prepare for, you need to hear this.
I already knew I was allergic to dust mites. That wasn't a mystery. I had been tested.
I knew they could make my breathing worse, so I did what you're supposed to do.
Hot wash the bedding, allergen proof mattress cover, vacuum, keep the humidity down, run the
purifier, follow the treatment plan. I did all of it, and still, there were nights I'd wake up coughing.
Sometimes I'd start clearing my throat the second I got into bed. Other nights I'd wake up mouth
breathing, or hear that little wheeze when I breathed out. On the bad nights, my chest would feel
tight enough that I'd sit up and wait for everything to calm down. So my bedroom slowly turned into
this whole breathing setup, AC at 68, purifier running. Fan pointed toward the bed, extra pillows
so I could sleep propped up. Whatever medication or spray I needed close enough to reach without
getting out of bed, I wasn't guessing anymore. I knew what I was allergic to.
I was just trying to get through the night without it turning into another 3am coughing fit.
Then one night, I'd done everything right. Fresh bedding, mattress cover zipped up,
room cleaned, purifier running, humidity where it was supposed to be. I went to sleep thinking,
okay, tonight should be fine. A few hours later, I woke up coughing so hard I had to sit straight up.
That little wheeze was back. My chest felt tight. And I remember looking around the room at everything
I'd bought, everything I'd washed, everything I was doing and thinking, how am I still here?
That was the part that got to me. I wasn't ignoring the problem. I wasn't being lazy about it.
I knew I had a dust mite allergy. And I was following me advice, but I was still building my nights
around managing what happened when I got into bed. So I started asking a different question.
Not, what am I allergic to? I knew that. I wanted to know, what are each of these things
actually doing about the dust mites in my mattress? And once I looked at it that way,

washing, covering, and cleaning. So I started researching what else I could do about the mattress
itself. Mattress vacuums came up first. That sounded obvious. Mites in the mattress? Vacuum the
mattress. So I looked into those. Then professional deep cleaning, different treatments.
